Subject: Geo DPA checkpoint: SCC -> UK IDTA mapping & evidence ask

Hi Ari —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, FinEdge is preparing to go live on our dedicated environment and your legal team requested a short packet of evidence and a mapping of how we will route EU/UK requests. To keep momentum, can you confirm the following on your side?

- Do you require us to execute the EU SCCs + UK IDTA (UK Addendum) or will the SCCs + a TIA/DTIA be sufficient for your European processing?
- Any required language your legal team needs in the DPA (e.g., logging retention caps, subprocessor notification windows)?
- If the UK IDTA is mandatory, do you expect us to complete the IDTA signature via DocuSign or your counter-signed PDF?

What we can provide this week:
- Redwood SCC template (redwood-scc-template-2028.docx)
- Current subprocessor register (subprocessor-register.csv)
- Short routing diagram and option matrix (we'll attach a lightweight diagram)

Would you and legal be comfortable if we share the above and a proposed TIA scope by end of day Thursday (2028-05-09)? If so I’ll include an exec summary for Laura and your legal counterpart.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Geo DPA checkpoint: SCC -> UK IDTA mapping & evidence ask

Ben —

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers from legal for planning: 

- FinEdge's compliance bar for EU->UK processing currently prefers execution of the EU SCCs plus the UK IDTA (UK Addendum) when data is routed from EU to UK. In limited cases a DTIA/TIA with additional technical controls has been accepted, but legal will want to review any mitigations before approving that path.
- Required DPA language: retention caps for logs (max 90 days unless otherwise justified), subprocessors must be pre-notified 10 business days, and we need clause covering on-demand audit evidence for transfers.
- Signature: legal prefers DocuSign for the IDTA; a counter-signed PDF is acceptable only for interim testing, but final production requires executed IDTA in DocuSign.

I'm attaching FinEdge's transfer questionnaire (FinEdge-Transfer-Questionnaire.pdf) which indicates specific fields they expect in a TIA submission. We can review your SCC template and subprocessor list after you share them; legal can provide redlines within 3 business days.

Best,
Ari
Ari Sharma | Head of Partnerships 
FinEdge Capital
ari.sharma@finedge.com

Laura

Quick technical note —

I reviewed the routing options and here's the condensed tradeoff: 

- UK-only processing (ingest and inference in a UK region): easiest from a legal standpoint but adds ~12-18% cost premium and could increase median latency for EU customers by ~20ms on our Dedicated pools.
- EU primary + UK fallback with selective token routing: lower cost but requires us to implement a per-account routing flag and enhanced KV-cache sharding to ensure no EU-origin PII persists on UK nodes. This is doable but we'll need a 2-week ops window and a short SOC2-style attestation for the caching behavior.

I'll attach a routing diagram and a checklist of controls we can show FinEdge to support a TIA (routing-diagram.png). If legal is open to a TIA with those mitigations, we can avoid an IDTA for now.

-Vivek
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
